gloss: to keep in mind; to bear in mind

definitions.gloss: to keep in mind; to bear in mind; to be mindful of
definitions.explanation: To consciously maintain awareness of something when making decisions or taking action. A somewhat formal expression used in both spoken and written Japanese.

examples.japanese: リスクを{念頭|ねんとう}に{置|お}く。
examples.english: To keep the risks in mind.

examples.japanese: {安全|あんぜん}を{念頭|ねんとう}に{置|お}いて{行動|こうどう}してください。
examples.english: Please act with safety in mind.

examples.japanese: {将来|しょうらい}の{成長|せいちょう}を{念頭|ねんとう}に{置|お}いた{投資|とうし}{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てることが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: It's important to create an investment plan that keeps future growth in mind.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
～を{念頭|ねんとう}に{置|お}く (to keep ~ in mind)
～を{念頭|ねんとう}に{置|お}いて (keeping ~ in mind — te-form used adverbially)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {安全|あんぜん}を{念頭|ねんとう}に{置|お}く (to keep safety in mind)
- リスクを{念頭|ねんとう}に{置|お}く (to keep risks in mind)
- {念頭|ねんとう}に{置|お}いた{上|うえ}で (with ~ in mind)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {頭|あたま}に{入|い}れておく: To make a mental note — more casual and colloquial.
- {心|こころ}がける: To try to, to be mindful of — implies active effort to maintain a habit or principle.
- {意識|いしき}する: To be conscious of — broader, can mean simply being aware without the deliberate planning nuance of {念頭|ねんとう}に{置|お}く.
